title: Redland City electoral division boundary sources
publisher: State of Queensland (Department of Natural Resources and Mines, Manufacturing and Regional and Rural Development); Electoral Commission of Queensland
boundaryEdition: 2024 current local-government division layer, retrieved 17 October 2026
boundaryCurrentness: The official current layer identifies all ten Redland features as election year 2024. ECQ's Redland-specific final determination remains the 2019 review. The current layer description identifies Bundaberg, Fraser Coast and Isaac as councils changed in the 2023 review; it warns that other councils' 2020 and 2024 spatial alignment may vary because of cadastre accuracy upgrades. Use this current service snapshot rather than tracing the historical 2019 overview image.
catalogueDataUpdatedMeaning: The portal's dataset date is separate from this retrieval date and the 2019 Redland review date. It does not establish that every Redland division was redrawn in 2024.

geometry.sourceDatasetCoordinateSystem: EPSG:4283 GDA94 geographic, as identified in layer sourceSpatialReference
geometry.deliveryCoordinateSystem: EPSG:4326 longitude, latitude, explicitly requested from the service
geometry.processing: The source GeoJSON response is retained byte-for-byte. No tracing, rounding, simplification, clipping, ring removal or invented geometry. The official service performs the requested coordinate transformation.

fields.elect_div: Source division label: DIVISION 1 through DIVISION 10. Use the division number with the parent council as the stable local route; it is not a nationwide identifier.
fields.div_name: Optional official division name. All ten Redland values are null; do not invent names.
fields.lga: Parent local-government name; REDLAND CITY for all ten features.
fields.elect_yr: Source election-year edition; 2024 for every returned Redland feature.
fields.act: Source legislative context; Local Government Act 2009.
fields.objectid: Source feature identifier. It may change when the service is republished and must not be used as the permanent public route.

displayRules: Use the same map, search, select, inspect and open interaction as the Queensland council map.
Render the exact supplied polygon rings on Canvas with no SVG tracing or replacement outlines.
Use a geographic raster beneath transparent division colours; division polygons include marine areas and must not be mistaken for land outlines.
Use the same projection for raster registration, geometry drawing and picking; preserve actual export extents.
Show the source boundary edition and retrieval date separately. Do not carry historical 2019 enrolment figures into current division profiles.
This is a dated navigational display, not an official address-to-division or voter-eligibility determination. Link to ECQ for official enquiries.
refreshRules: Check the ECQ Redland review page and divisional-review programme for a newer determination.
Check the official current layer 7 metadata and query REDLAND CITY with outSR=4326. Do not use superseded layer 11 or assume native coordinates are longitude and latitude.
Retain the complete downloaded response, record a new checksum, and verify divisions 1 through 10 exactly once unless an official arrangement change authorises a different set.
Validate closed rings, all coordinate pairs and source edition attributes; test mainland and island selection after any data or projection change.
Record the real update date and source changes in the local history. Update routes, captions and agent rules when an official boundary change takes effect.
